name: Banana Reef
current_notes: Generally gentle to moderate and considered beginner-friendly, but can turn strong at times, with occasional turbulence around the reef's overhangs.
marine_life_notes: Groupers, sharks, jacks, blue-striped snapper and barracuda commonly seen among the coral formations; turtles are seen occasionally.
notes: Source: padi.com dive-site listing, Wikipedia 'Diving in the Maldives', and multiple dive-operator guides (maldives-magazine.com, amaldives.com, extrememaldives.com). One of the Maldives' original, most famous reef dives, officially named Gaathugiri, a ~300m banana-shaped reef in North Male Atoll roughly 20 minutes by speedboat from Male. Sources tie it generally to the North Male Atoll area (mentioned alongside Hulhumale, Thulusdhoo and Maafushi as nearby islands) without singling out one specific nearest inhabited/resort island from our dataset with confidence, so nearby_island_name was left null rather than guessed.

name: HP Reef
current_notes: Strong currents are common, especially during the southwest monsoon; recommended for advanced divers.
marine_life_notes: Grey reef sharks, eagle rays, barracuda, dog-toothed tuna and various angelfish/bannerfish species; manta rays are seen occasionally. Soft corals, gorgonian fans and sea whips cover the reef top.
notes: Source: divedesk.mv, mindtrip.ai summary, wanderon.in and other dive-site guides. Also known locally as Girifushi Thila, a submerged pinnacle designated a Marine Protected Area near Himmafushi Island, North Male Atoll, with caves, crevices and a vertical swim-through 'chimney' reaching ~25m. Some sources use 'Rainbow Reef' as an alternate name for this same site, while a separate resort listing (Gili Lankanfushi's dive centre) names 'HP Reef' and 'Rainbow Reef' as two distinct sites on its trip roster -- given this naming ambiguity, no separate 'Rainbow Reef' entry was added to this file to avoid a possible duplicate.

name: Lankan Manta Point
current_notes: Moderate to strong current at the outer-reef cleaning stations; divers are recommended to be comfortable with current and drift diving.
marine_life_notes: Manta rays are commonly seen at the site's cleaning stations, with sources describing daily sightings in peak season (roughly mid-August through November) and year-round presence with a second reported peak Nov-May; never described as guaranteed.
notes: Source: divessi.com dive-guide entry, zubludiving.com manta/whale-shark season article, liveaboard.com and amaldives.com guides. A gently sloping reef on the southeast outer reef of Lankanfinolhu island (North Male Atoll) with three manta cleaning stations (shallow ~15m, deeper ~25m). Lankanfinolhu itself is not one of our dataset's inhabited/resort islands, but Gili Lankanfushi's own dive centre (Ocean Paradise) lists Manta Point among the named sites it runs trips to, so nearby_island_name is set to 'Lankanfushi' on that basis. experience_level left null since no source used one of the standard beginner/intermediate/advanced labels for this specific site, only current-comfort guidance.

name: Fish Head (Mushimasmingili Thila)
current_notes: Forceful tidal currents that can range from moderate to powerful, making it a thrilling drift dive; not recommended for novice divers.
marine_life_notes: Notable for a consistent, often large presence of grey reef sharks (sometimes reported in groups of 20+) patrolling the deeper sections, along with whitetip reef sharks and abundant reef fish.
notes: Source: scubadivingearth.com, maldivestour.guide, maldivespostcards.com, amaldives.com and dive.site listings. An oval reef pinnacle (~100m x 60m) in North Ari Atoll (also called Ari Atoll), between the islands of Mandhoo and Maamingili/Maamgili (spelling varies by source) -- both real islands in Alif Dhaalu Atoll in our dataset; Maamingili was used as nearby_island_name. Depth figures vary somewhat by source (reef top 5-8m; general slope described as 8-20m then to 42m on the south side by one source, versus a simpler 'rises from 30m to 5m below surface' by another) -- the more consistently repeated 5m/30m range was used here, with the deeper south-side figure noted as a variant rather than used directly.

name: Kuda Rah Thila
current_notes: Strong, swirling incoming current makes this an advanced dive.
marine_life_notes: Densely covered in soft coral and sea fans; frequented by groupers, snapper, fusiliers, trevally, reef sharks and eagle rays.
notes: Source: padi.com dive-site listing, resortlife.travel, nova-maldives.com, southaridivecenter.com and other South Ari Atoll dive guides. The most famous dive site in South Ari Atoll (a marine protected area since 1995), a small thila in the Dhigurah/Dhigurahfaru channel about 1km from Kudarah island. Kudarah/Kuda Rah is an uninhabited resort island, not one of the islands already in our dataset, so nearby_island_name was left null rather than guessed onto a nearby but not source-confirmed island (e.g. Dhigurah).

name: Guraidhoo Kandu
current_notes: Strong currents suitable only for advanced, experienced divers; can pull divers off the reef, with frequent underwater turbulence. December-May usually brings the clearest channel conditions.
marine_life_notes: Grey reef sharks are common when the current is incoming, along with eagle rays, jacks, tuna, barracuda, turtles, snappers and fusiliers.
notes: Source: dive-the-world.com South Male Atoll guide, divebooker.com listing for 'Guraidho Kandu', and en.wikipedia.org 'Fushi Kandu' context. A channel dive south of Guraidhoo island (Kaafu Atoll, a real inhabited island already in our dataset), consisting of two channels and a central reef; strongest fish/shark activity reported around 35m at the drop-off. depth_min_meters left null since no source gave a shallow-end figure distinct from the general channel/reef-plateau description.

name: Kandooma Thila
current_notes: Strong outgoing current runs west to east through the channel between the thila and the reef; suitable only for experienced divers.
marine_life_notes: A focal point for eagle rays, dogtooth tuna, bluefin trevally and loose groups of grey reef sharks (sometimes 50+ in favorable current); also whitetip sharks and green turtles. A shark cleaning station is the site's main attraction.
notes: Source: padi.com dive-site listing (titled 'Cocoa Thila'), tribloo.com, wikibubbles.com and awesomeasiatravel.com. A teardrop-shaped pinnacle just outside Kandooma island in South Male Atoll, depths reported 12-40m (top of the thila at ~16m on its west/north side). Kandooma is an uninhabited resort island, not one of the islands already in our dataset, so nearby_island_name was left null rather than guessed onto a nearby but not source-confirmed island.

name: Maaya Thila
current_notes: Current is highly changeable: in little or no current the site can suit all diver levels, but conditions are often unstable/unpredictable and it is then unsuitable for novice-level divers, so crew judgment on the day matters.
marine_life_notes: Famous as a night-dive site for actively hunting whitetip reef sharks; by day and night also hosts grey reef sharks (sometimes numbering into the teens), turtles, moray eels, stingrays, frogfish, teira batfish and blue-faced angelfish.
notes: Source: padi.com dive-site listing, resortlife.travel, divemagazine.com feature on Ari Atoll thilas, and scubaportal.it. A circular Marine Protected Area pinnacle (~80m across) in North Ari Atoll, rising from ~30m to within 6m of the surface. experience_level left null given the source's own explicit description of highly variable suitability rather than one fixed label; nearby_island_name left null as no source tied it to one specific inhabited/resort island from our dataset.

name: Rasdhoo Madivaru
current_notes: Strong currents are common; treated as an advanced, current-sensitive drift dive along the outer atoll wall.
marine_life_notes: Best known for resident scalloped hammerhead sharks (typically seen on early-dawn dives, no strong seasonality reported), plus jacks, barracuda, tuna, whitetip and grey reef sharks, and eagle rays.
notes: Source: divessi.com ('Hammerhead Shark Point'), dive-the-world.com Rasdhoo guide, splashpacker.com, divejourney.io and divebooker.com. A channel at the intersection of Rasdhoo and Madivaru (Rasdhoo is a real inhabited island, atoll capital of Alif Alif Atoll, already in our dataset). Also widely called 'Hammerhead Point' or 'Madivaru Corner'. Hammerhead sightings are described as an 'opportunity' on dawn dives rather than guaranteed, consistent with the task's hedging rule.

name: Kuda Giri Wreck
current_notes: Generally very little current at this site.
marine_life_notes: Colorful sponges, tube corals and orange cup corals cover the wreck; batfish, glassfish, gobies, shrimp and triggerfish are common, with turtles, wrasses, eels and octopus also reported.
notes: Source: divehappy.com, zentacle.com, scubadivingearth.com and wannadive.net. A no-name shipwreck (also referenced as 'MS Azieta') resting upright next to the Kuda Giri pinnacle in South Male Atoll, near Gulhi island (a real inhabited island already in our dataset). Penetration is possible in a few places. Exact sinking history/date not found in snippets reviewed, so omitted; experience_level left null as no source used one of the standard difficulty labels for this specific site, only the low-current observation.

name: Okobe Thila
current_notes: Current conditions mean the site is considered necessary for experienced divers when exploring North Male Atoll.
marine_life_notes: Bluestripe snapper, oriental sweetlips and fusiliers school around the reef's north end; barracuda, Napoleon wrasse, tuna, trevally and white-tip reef sharks are also reported, amid dense soft coral cover.
notes: Source: scubago.com dive-site listing and general North Male Atoll dive guides (dive-the-world.com, euro-divers.com). A marine-protected, three-pinnacle site in southeast North Male Atoll. Not tied to one specific inhabited island by these general guides, but Gili Lankanfushi's own dive centre (Ocean Paradise) lists Okobe Thila among the named sites it runs trips to, so nearby_island_name is set to 'Lankanfushi' on that basis, the same reasoning used for Lankan Manta Point above.

name: Vaadhoo Caves
current_notes: Current is usually light, which also makes the area popular for snorkeling.
marine_life_notes: Spectacular soft coral growth and abundant fish life on the southwest side of the house reef; the nearby channel occasionally brings in pelagic visitors such as eagle rays, mobula rays, tuna and grey reef sharks.
notes: Source: en.wikipedia.org 'Vaadhoo Caves', padi.com ('Male Caves Divesite'), divebooker.com and scubadivingearth.com. Located on the northwest outer reef of Vaadhoo island, South Male Atoll, with a network of small caves and one larger cave with a swim-through passage, rated by one source as suitable for PADI Intermediate-level recreational divers (used directly as experience_level). Vaadhoo island itself is not one of the islands already in our dataset, so nearby_island_name was left null rather than guessed onto a different, nearby-but-unconfirmed island.
